features.feature_value: Would remove only when implied/encouraged threats of violence appear; otherwise allow expression.
features.evidence_span: implied or encouraged threats of violence
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states violence-related threat content is the criterion for removal.

features.feature_value: Allows if making a point but not if it becomes name-calling/viciously attacking a person or group.
features.evidence_span: not just name-calling or viciously attacking a person or group of people
features.rationale: They describe a boundary between acceptable argumentation and unacceptable personal/group attacks.

features.feature_value: Used specific profanity words/length cues as a deciding factor (e.g., certain sex-act or insult terms) to cross the line.
features.evidence_span: Four letter words for a sex act
features.rationale: They tie decisions to particular profane word types and lengths.

features.feature_value: Removes pairs when foul language is used, especially when it seems someone is targeted with curse words; free speech but curb harassment.
features.evidence_span: Attacking someone with curse words isn't needed
features.rationale: They state foul language targeting/attacking drove removal despite valuing free speech.

features.feature_value: Decision based on whether anything felt threatening; if no red flags/threats, keep.
features.evidence_span: Didn't see anything that raised a red flag
features.rationale: They explicitly use absence of threatening cues as the basis for their keep/remove decision.

features.feature_value: Claims their decision was not really influenced; believes people are entitled to their opinions without judgment.
features.rationale: They directly attribute minimal impact from the pair and rely on a general norm about opinions.

features.feature_value: Accepts free speech generally but removes when misinformation is presented as truth, plus removes violence-directed content.
features.evidence_span: misinformation described as truth is not
features.rationale: They set a substantive criterion for removal beyond violence: misinformation framed as truth.

features.feature_value: Kept posts that made an argument/meaningful opinion; only removed when close to a death-threat or otherwise less substantive.
features.evidence_span: made an argument or expressed a meaningful opinion
features.rationale: They use argument quality as the main rule, with an edge-case removal tied to threat-likeness.
